headline: Florida's early vote is R+1.0 by registration on 3.52 million ballots in the Oct 27 file (Republicans up 158,000 in person, Democrats up 123,000 by mail), still better for Democrats than R+5.3 at seven days out in 2022; the official same-point comparison across five states implies a national vote of about D-0.8 (±1.2) against 2022 and about D+5.0 (±1.5) against 2024, while the polls say D+8.6 and the app's forecast D+6.8. Nevada is D+5.6 against D+2.2 in 2022, Colorado D+7.9 against D+3.8, Iowa's absentee pool D+13.7 against D+22.4 and Pennsylvania's mail D+40.9 against D+50.4. The news comparisons lean Democratic: Jon Ralston has Clark County's Democratic lead above 43,000 ballots (almost 13 points) against under 29,000 (under 7 points) at this stage in 2022, North Carolina is 37% ahead of 2022 at 1.77 million ballots, Georgia passed 2 million in-person votes with turnout matching 2022's same-point pace, Texas's Democratic-primary voters lead Republican-primary voters by 115,000 where Republicans led by 400,000 in 2022, and Wisconsin's and Michigan's absentee returns have moved ahead of 2022.

measures.src: Florida Division of Elections daily file via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
measures.aff: Official data. 3,517,675 ballots in the Oct 27 file (mail 1,583,248, in person 1,934,427) vs. the state's figures at seven days out in 2024; 2024 is a presidential baseline in which Republicans had moved to in-person voting. Against 2022 the same file reads R+1.0 vs. R+5.3

measures.aff: Official data. 495,447 ballots through Oct 27's file (mail 290,304, in person 205,143) vs. Ralston's count at seven days out in 2024 (Republicans up 5.5); 2022 at the same point was D+2.2

measures.label: Colorado: returned ballots by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Colorado Secretary of State daily ballot-return release via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
measures.aff: Official data. 982,530 ballots through Oct 27 vs. 1,436,325 at seven days out in 2024; 2022 at the same point was D+3.8

measures.label: Iowa: absentee ballots received by registration, D-minus-R margin
measures.src: Iowa Secretary of State daily absentee report via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
measures.aff: Official data. 112,635 absentee ballots received in the Oct 27 report vs. the state's report at the same point in 2024; 2022 at the same point was D+22.4, and Iowa Democrats vote absentee far more than Republicans in every year

measures.src: Pennsylvania Department of State daily mail-ballot report via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
measures.aff: Official data. 893,224 ballots returned through Oct 27 vs. about 1.49 million at the same point in 2024 (interpolated); no in-person early voting, and the mail pool is lopsidedly Democratic every year (D+50.4 at this point in 2022)

measures.src: News 5 Cleveland, Oct 13 (Ohio Secretary of State data)

compare_note: Registered-party margin among early ballots, 2026 vs. the same point in 2024. Florida, Nevada, Colorado, Iowa and Pennsylvania are computed from the state files by the update job (Florida 3,517,675 ballots in the Oct 27 file against the state's 2024 figures at seven days out; Nevada 495,447 against Ralston's 2024 count; Colorado 982,530 through Oct 27; Iowa 112,635 absentees in the Oct 27 report; Pennsylvania 893,224 mail ballots through Oct 27); Maine is Call the Map's reading of the state file (174,765 ballots through Oct 22). Virginia's early voters are 63% Democratic on L2's modeled two-party split, vs. 59% at the same point in 2024 (Morris, Oct 12); Ohio's early voters were 41% Democratic and 28% Republican by last primary ballot as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024 (News 5 Cleveland, from Secretary of State data). Every state with party registration is more Democratic than at this point in 2024, Florida most of all because 2024's Republicans had moved to in-person early voting; against 2022 the official comparison is narrower and mixed (Florida R+1.0 vs. R+5.3, Nevada D+5.6 vs. D+2.2, Colorado D+7.9 vs. D+3.8, Iowa D+13.7 vs. D+22.4, Pennsylvania D+40.9 vs. D+50.4), and North Carolina's comparison is computed from the State Board's files.

bullets.title: The official comparison with 2022 covers five states and implies a national vote of about D-0.8; against 2024 it reads about D+5.0.
bullets.html: By registration, Florida's Oct 27 file counts 3,517,675 ballots at R+1.0 (mail 683,404 Democrats to 560,127 Republicans; in person 693,653 to 851,414), against R+5.3 at seven days out in 2022 (the state's Nov 1, 2022 figures); Nevada's 495,447 ballots are D+5.6 (mail D+33,780, in person R+6,036) against D+2.2 on the same day in 2022; Colorado's 982,530 returned ballots are D+7.9 against D+3.8; Iowa's 112,635 absentees are D+13.7 against D+22.4; and Pennsylvania's 893,224 returned mail ballots are D+40.9 against D+50.4. The app's calibrated slopes turn those into +3.7, +2.9, +3.4, -1.9 and -2.1 points of margin and a pooled implied national vote of about D-0.8 (±1.2), against polls at D+8.6 and the app's forecast at D+6.8; the Oct 26 files read D-0.7 on the same five states. Against 2024 the same files read better for Democrats: Florida R+1.0 against R+11.6 (worth about +9.0), Nevada D+5.6 against R+5.5 (+9.4) and Colorado D+7.9 against D+2.2 (+4.8) pool to about D+5.0 (±1.5); Pennsylvania's mail at D+40.9 against D+25.5 is worth about +3.4 (±3.5) and Iowa's D+13.7 against D+1.8 about +2.7 (±3.4). Arizona's county compilation reads R+0.7 on 971,184 ballots with no same-point baseline.
sources: Florida Division of Elections via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
UF Election Lab daily file (Nevada, Oct 27)
Pennsylvania Department of State daily mail-ballot report via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
CBS Miami/News Service of Florida, Oct 31, 2022 (the 2022 Florida baseline)

bullets.title: Nevada: Clark County's Democratic lead passed 43,000 ballots Tuesday night (almost 13 points) against under 29,000 (under 7) at this stage in 2022.
bullets.html: Jon Ralston's 9 p.m. Oct 27 entry: Democrats 'have gained 3,500 voters today' and 'increased their percentage lead by a tenth of a point,' with 'the D lead above 43,000 ballots in Clark with a week to go' and the firewall 'almost 13 percent right now,' against a 2022 Clark firewall that was 'under 29,000' and under 7 percent (47,000, or 11 percent, in 2018); more than 8,000 Clark mail ballots were waiting to be accepted, and Republicans 'fought in-person voting to a virtual draw.' His 7 a.m. entry (through Monday): statewide 'D+24,395, or 6 percent' on about 444,000 ballots, 'so about 700,000 are likely left'; Democrats 178,515 votes (72.3% from Clark), Republicans 154,120 (59.2% Clark, 21.1% rurals), others 111,607, 'lower than most people have forecast'; turnout of registration 31% for Democrats, 27% for Republicans, 12% for the rest; Clark 300,806 ballots with a 38,207 lead (12.7 points) 'against 20,880 (7.9 points) in 2022,' in person D+4,643 (R+14,932 then) and mail D+33,564 (D+35,812 then); Washoe about 20% of the vote, the rurals 13%. He expects 'a 30,000-ballot lead by Saturday and maybe as high as 40,000 before Election Day,' and his 2022-based model has Republicans winning the rurals by about 56,000 ballots. The state's Oct 27 file reads D+5.6 on 495,447 ballots against D+2.2 at this point in 2022 and R+5.5 in 2024.
sources: UF Election Lab daily file (Nevada, Oct 27)
bullets.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; county and Secretary of State data

bullets.title: North Carolina's early vote is 37% ahead of 2022 at 1.77 million ballots; Democrats are 41% of them, Republicans 25%.
bullets.html: The State Board of Elections' Oct 27 release, as reported by ABC11 and WLOS: 1,773,889 ballots cast through Monday Oct 26, 'about 37% more than at the same point in 2022'; Democrats nearly 41%, unaffiliated voters just under 35%, Republicans nearly 25%. Black voters are nearly 22% of ballots against slightly over 19% of registrants; Hispanic voters slightly over 3% against about 4.7% of registrants, though Michael Bitzer notes the in-person Hispanic share is 'more than double the 1.3% at the same point in 2022.' Wake County leads with more than 222,000 ballots; Buncombe has more than 63,000. Call the Map's reading of the Oct 26 file: Democrats 726,638 (up 43% on 2022), Republicans 430,032 (up 6%), unaffiliated 617,220 (up 60%), a D+16.7 gap against D+8.0. Early voting ends Saturday Oct 31 at 3 p.m. The app's own file carries the official comparison (1,773,890 ballots against 1,298,679 at eight days out in 2022).
sources: WLOS (State Board of Elections release), Oct 28
Call the Map (NC State Board of Elections file), Oct 27
bullets.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets; Call the Map is an independent tracker

bullets.title: Georgia passed 2 million in-person votes with turnout at 28%, matching 2022's pace at the same point; mail voting is down by half.
bullets.html: The Secretary of State's Oct 27 release (4:30 p.m.): 2,000,452 in-person early votes and 97,382 accepted absentee ballots, statewide turnout 28% with seven days left, which 'matches the 2022 figure at the same point'; the in-person count is already '22% above' 2022's full 15-day total of 1,640,652. Raffensperger: voters 'are shattering in-person turnout records because they trust our election process.' The AJC's analysis (Oct 27): about 2 million voted, roughly 7% ahead of the same point in 2022 on GeorgiaVotes' count; mail voting is down more than 50% from the same point in 2022; at least 360,000 early voters (nearly one in five) did not vote in 2022, and about 244,000 of 2022's Election Day voters have already voted; white voters are about 53% of early voters but 41% of those who skipped 2022; voters 50 and over are nearly three-quarters, the under-30s about 9%; Athens-Clarke is about a third ahead of 2022 and the Harris counties are further ahead than the Trump counties. Georgia has no party registration; early voting ends Oct 30.
sources: Atlanta News First (Secretary of State release), Oct 27

bullets.title: Texas: 5.1 million have voted, and Democratic-primary voters lead Republican-primary voters by 115,000 where Republicans led by 400,000 in 2022.
bullets.html: Republican data consultant Derek Ryan, as reported by NBC 5 (Oct 27): more than 4.5 million voted in the first seven days; among them, voters with a Democratic primary history led those with a Republican one by 115,000, against a Republican lead of 400,000 at the same point in the last midterm; about 2 million reliable Republican primary voters had not yet voted; slightly more women than men, slightly more under-45s than in 2022, and 'Hispanic turnout is roughly 3% higher than four years ago'; he expects about 10 million votes in all and 'a very long night.' theoelections' count through Oct 27: 5,137,795 voted (4,904,201 in person, 233,594 by mail); in-person ballots 31.9% from Democratic-primary-only voters, 32.3% Republican-only, 32.8% with no primary history; the mail 35.2% to 26.5%. Through Oct 23 the Democratic-primary lead was 75,000 and nearly two-thirds of four-of-four Democratic primary voters had voted, with 318,000 four-of-four Republicans still out (The Texan). Texas has no party registration; early voting ends Oct 30.
bullets.aff: Derek Ryan is a Republican consultant; theoelections is an independent tracker whose affiliation is not stated; The Texan is a conservative-leaning outlet

bullets.title: Florida: R+1.0 in the Oct 27 file, with Republicans up 158,000 in person and Democrats up 123,000 by mail.
bullets.html: The Division of Elections' Oct 27 file (the app's official comparison) has 1,934,427 in-person ballots, 851,414 Republican to 693,653 Democratic (R+157,761), and 1,583,248 mail ballots returned, 683,404 Democratic to 560,127 Republican (D+123,277): 40.1% Republican to 39.1% Democratic on 3,517,675 ballots, from R+0.4 on 3,152,810 in the Oct 26 file and D+6.7 at twenty days out. WFLA's reading of the 8:07 a.m. Oct 27 snapshot had Republicans ahead by 12,766 (1,257,198 to 1,244,432) with 986,535 mail ballots outstanding; Democrats led the mail in Miami-Dade (59,105 to 42,666), Broward, Palm Beach and Orange, Republicans the in-person vote in Miami-Dade (63,167 to 58,612) and Lee. Political Cortadito's Miami-Dade count through Sunday: 263,034 ballots, Democrats 102,556 to 92,858 overall but Republicans ahead in person by 4,170; 22.9% of registered Democrats and 18.3% of Republicans had voted. At seven days out in 2022 the state was R+5.3 (the app's baseline from the state's Nov 1 figures, 3.30 million ballots), and at the same point in 2024 R+11.6.
sources: Florida Division of Elections via the app's official comparison, Oct 27
CBS Miami/News Service of Florida, Oct 31, 2022
bullets.aff: Official data; Political Cortadito is an independent Miami political blog

bullets.title: Turnout without party: Wisconsin's absentee returns are 2% ahead of 2022, Michigan's 4% ahead plus 216,000 in-person votes, Virginia's early vote has passed 2022's final total, Pennsylvania's mail is 1% behind.
bullets.html: Wisconsin: the Elections Commission's report a week out has 513,602 absentee ballots returned (251,092 of them in person) against 503,180 at the same point in 2022 (FOX 11, Oct 27); the last county breakdown (Oct 23) had Milwaukee County down 10.1% and Dane down 14.9% while Waukesha and Washington were up. Michigan: 1,392,170 ballots as of 7 a.m. Oct 27, 18.8% of active voters, 1,176,375 absentee ballots returned (2,154,870 requested) and 215,795 early in-person votes, against 1,126,246 absentee ballots returned and 1,899,273 requested a week before Election Day 2022 (Secretary of State). Virginia: 1,183,919 early ballots as of Oct 26 per VPAP, about three-quarters in person, against 976,558 in all of 2022's early period (DC News Now). Pennsylvania: 890,103 mail ballots returned, 1% below the same point in 2022, Democrats 585,487 (down 9%), Republicans 221,028 (up 20%), unaffiliated 83,588 (up 10%); D+40.9 against D+50.8 (Call the Map's Oct 27 reading). Ohio: 68% of absentee ballots returned a week out, with Secretary of State LaRose saying the state 'could be on track to break another record' (NBC4).
sources: Dairyland Sentinel (Wisconsin Elections Commission data), Oct 23
bullets.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets and an independent tracker; Dairyland Sentinel's analysis is by a former Republican legislator

bullets.title: Nationally, 35 million have voted; UF's count in the registration states is about 45% Democrats to 30% Republicans, and McDonald says every state he has checked but Pennsylvania and Tennessee is ahead of 2022.
bullets.html: UF Election Lab counted 35,140,289 ballots across 49 reporting jurisdictions in the app's Oct 28 file. Michael McDonald (via TNND, Oct 26): more than 30 million ballots as of Monday afternoon; in the states with party registration about 45% Democrats, 30% Republicans and 25% unaffiliated or other; about half in person and half by mail, with nearly 60 million mail ballots requested and nearly 15 million returned; 'Every other state where I've done this analysis, it's pacing ahead' of 2022 except Pennsylvania and Tennessee; Hispanic voters are 'voting at unprecedented numbers.' Call the Map's Oct 27 tally is 30,500,747 in 46 states, with its six day-aligned states (North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Maine, Nevada, Iowa and Florida) 12% ahead of 2022 and five of the six up. Pluribus News (Oct 23): L2's modeled figures 49% Democrats to 34% Republicans, nearly 60% of early voters over 65, and L2's Paul Westcott: 'The best comparison is 2022, and 2022 was not a blue wave.' The shift from mail to in person continues: Georgia's mail is down by half, Florida's in-person vote is 55% of the total and Republican by 158,000, Wisconsin's in-person absentee ballots are almost half its returns, Michigan took 216,000 in-person votes in its first days.
bullets.aff: McDonald is a nonpartisan academic; L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor whose party figures are modeled in states without registration; Pluribus and TNND are nonpartisan

calendar_note: Kentucky's early in-person voting runs Oct 29-31; it is the last battleground opening. Closing dates: Maine's no-excuse absentee period Oct 29; Georgia, Texas, Nevada and Arizona Oct 30; North Carolina Oct 31 (3 p.m.); Michigan and Wisconsin Nov 1; Nebraska's in-person early voting Nov 2. Pennsylvania and New Hampshire have no early in-person voting.
cast_at_note: Ballots counted (UF Election Lab, 49 jurisdictions reporting, state data as of Oct 23-27) when these comparisons were compiled; sets the automatic early-vote weight.
signals_verdict: The official same-point comparison with 2022 (Florida, Nevada, Colorado, Iowa and Pennsylvania) implies a national vote of about D-0.8 (±1.2): Florida is R+1.0 by registration in the Oct 27 file against R+5.3 at seven days out in 2022, Nevada D+5.6 against D+2.2, Colorado D+7.9 against D+3.8, Iowa's absentee pool D+13.7 against D+22.4 and Pennsylvania's mail D+40.9 against D+50.4; against 2024, Florida (R+1.0 vs. R+11.6), Nevada (D+5.6 vs. R+5.5) and Colorado pool to about D+5.0 (±1.5), so the early vote fits a Democratic year without confirming polls at D+8.6. The news comparisons are bluer: Ralston has Clark County's Democratic lead above 43,000 ballots (almost 13 points) against under 29,000 (under 7) at this stage in 2022, North Carolina is 37% ahead of 2022 at 1.77 million ballots with Republicans a quarter of them, Georgia's turnout matches 2022's same-point pace with in-person voting past 2 million, Texas's Democratic-primary voters lead by 115,000 where Republican-primary voters led by 400,000 in 2022, and Wisconsin's and Michigan's absentee returns have moved ahead of 2022, while Florida's in-person vote is Republican by 158,000 and Pennsylvania's mail trails 2022. The next tests are how far Florida's Republican margin grows in the final three days of in-person voting, Nevada's last three days before early voting closes Oct 30, the closing surge in Georgia and Texas through Oct 30 and North Carolina through Oct 31, and whether Pennsylvania's mail returns catch 2022.

signals.title: Clark County's Democratic lead passed 43,000 ballots Tuesday night, almost 13 points, against under 29,000 (under 7) at this stage in 2022
signals.value: Jon Ralston, 9 p.m. Oct 27: Democrats 'have gained 3,500 voters today,' 'the D lead above 43,000 ballots in Clark with a week to go,' the firewall 'almost 13 percent right now' against 'under 29,000' and under 7 percent at this point in 2022 (47,000, 11 percent, in 2018); 8,000 Clark mail ballots still to be accepted; Republicans 'fought in-person voting to a virtual draw.' 7 a.m. (through Monday): statewide 'D+24,395, or 6 percent' on about 444,000 ballots; Clark 300,806 ballots, D+38,207 (12.7 points) 'against 20,880 (7.9 points) in 2022,' in person D+4,643 (R+14,932 then), mail D+33,564 (D+35,812 then); turnout 31% of Democrats, 27% of Republicans, 12% of others; non-major-party ballots 111,607, 'lower than most people have forecast.' He expects 'a 30,000-ballot lead by Saturday and maybe as high as 40,000 before Election Day.'
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice. The Democratic edge is the mail; the in-person vote is a draw and Republicans won Election Day 2022 by nearly 50,000 ballots, and his model has them winning the rurals by about 56,000. About 700,000 votes are still to come. The state's Oct 27 file reads D+5.6 on 495,447 ballots against D+2.2 at this point in 2022 and R+5.5 in 2024 (the app's official panel).
signals.aff: Nonpartisan outlet (Jon Ralston); county and Secretary of State data

signals.title: North Carolina's early vote is 37% ahead of 2022 at 1.77 million ballots; Democrats are 41% of them, Republicans 25%
signals.value: State Board of Elections release of Oct 27 (via ABC11 and WLOS): 1,773,889 ballots through Monday Oct 26, 'about 37% more than at the same point in 2022'; Democrats nearly 41%, unaffiliated just under 35%, Republicans nearly 25%; Black voters nearly 22% of ballots against about 19% of registrants; Wake County above 222,000. Call the Map's reading of the Oct 26 file: Democrats 726,638 (+43% on 2022), Republicans 430,032 (+6%), unaffiliated 617,220 (+60%), D+16.7 against D+8.0.
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice, and much of the Democratic surge is 2022 Election Day voters moving earlier; Republicans outvoted Democrats on Election Day 2022. Hispanic voters are 3% of ballots against 4.7% of registrants. Early voting ends Oct 31 at 3 p.m. The app's own file carries the official comparison.
signals.src: ABC11, Oct 27; WLOS, Oct 28; Call the Map, Oct 27
signals.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets; Call the Map is an independent tracker

signals.title: Georgia passed 2 million in-person votes; turnout of 28% matches 2022's same-point pace, and the AJC has the count 7% ahead with Harris counties leading
signals.value: Secretary of State release, Oct 27 (4:30 p.m.): 2,000,452 in-person early votes and 97,382 accepted absentee ballots; turnout 28% with seven days left, which 'matches the 2022 figure at the same point'; the in-person count is 22% above 2022's full 15-day total (1,640,652). AJC (Oct 27): about 7% ahead of the same point in 2022 on GeorgiaVotes' count; mail voting down more than 50%; at least 360,000 early voters (nearly one in five) skipped 2022, and about 244,000 of 2022's Election Day voters have voted; the Harris counties are further ahead of 2022 than the Trump counties, Athens-Clarke about a third ahead. TargetSmart's model (Oct 26) put the early electorate at 54% Democratic-aligned, 41% Republican-aligned.
signals.catch: Georgia has no party registration, so the direction comes from geography and a Democratic-aligned vendor's model; the same-point turnout match means the surge is mostly mail voters moving in person. The electorate is old (voters 50 and over are nearly three-quarters, the under-30s about 9%). Early voting ends Oct 30.
signals.src: Atlanta News First, Oct 27; AJC, Oct 27
signals.aff: Official data via nonpartisan outlets; TargetSmart is a Democratic-aligned vendor (modeled party)

signals.title: Texas: Democratic-primary voters lead Republican-primary voters by 115,000 where Republicans led by 400,000 at this point in 2022; 5.1 million have voted
signals.value: Republican data consultant Derek Ryan via NBC 5 (Oct 27): after seven days, voters with a Democratic primary history led those with a Republican one by 115,000, against a Republican lead of 400,000 at the same point in the last midterm; about 2 million reliable Republican primary voters had not yet voted; 'Hispanic turnout is roughly 3% higher than four years ago'; he expects about 10 million votes. theoelections through Oct 27: 5,137,795 voted; in-person ballots 31.9% Democratic-primary-only, 32.3% Republican-only, 32.8% no primary; mail 35.2% to 26.5%. Through Oct 23, nearly two-thirds of four-of-four Democratic primary voters had voted and 318,000 four-of-four Republicans had not (The Texan).
signals.catch: No party registration: 'party' is primary history, and 2022's electorate was unusually Republican. Ryan's 2 million unvoted Republican primary voters are the Republican closing argument, and he expects 20-30% of all votes in the final three days.
signals.src: NBC 5 DFW, Oct 27; theoelections, Oct 27; The Texan, Oct 26
signals.aff: Derek Ryan is a Republican consultant; theoelections is an independent tracker whose affiliation is not stated; The Texan is conservative-leaning

signals.title: Florida's combined early vote is R+1.0 in the Oct 27 file, with Republicans up 158,000 in person and widening by about 30,000 a day
signals.value: Division of Elections file for Oct 27 (the app's official panel): 1,934,427 in-person ballots, 851,414 Republican to 693,653 Democratic (R+157,761, from R+125,966 on the 8 a.m. Oct 27 snapshot and R+94,750 on Oct 25); 1,583,248 mail ballots returned, 683,404 Democratic to 560,127 Republican (D+123,277). Combined: 40.1% Republican to 39.1% Democratic on 3,517,675 ballots, from R+0.4 on Oct 26 and D+6.7 at twenty days out. Political Cortadito's Miami-Dade count through Sunday: Democrats ahead overall 102,556 to 92,858 but Republicans ahead in person by 4,170.
signals.catch: The same-point comparison still favors Democrats: R+5.3 at seven days out in 2022 and R+11.6 in 2024 (the app's official panel), and 2022's final early vote was R+6.7. Republicans won Florida's in-person vote by far more in both years; 986,535 mail ballots were still outstanding on Oct 27, most of them Democratic or unaffiliated. Registration is not vote choice.
signals.src: Florida Division of Elections daily file via the app's official comparison, Oct 27; WFLA, Oct 27; Political Cortadito, Oct 26
signals.aff: Official data; Political Cortadito is an independent Miami political blog

signals.title: Pennsylvania's mail returns trail 2022 by 1%, with Democrats' returns down 9% and Republicans' up 20%
signals.value: Call the Map (Oct 27 reading of the state file): 890,103 mail ballots returned, 1% below the same point in 2022; Democrats 585,487 (down 9%), Republicans 221,028 (up 20%), unaffiliated 83,588 (up 10%); D+40.9 vs. D+50.8. The state's Oct 27 file: 893,224 returned of 1,277,342 approved; the app's official panel reads D+40.9 against D+50.4 at this point in 2022 and D+25.5 in 2024. Michael McDonald (TNND, Oct 26) names Pennsylvania and Tennessee as the only states he has checked that are not pacing ahead of 2022.
signals.catch: Pennsylvania's mail vote is lopsidedly Democratic every year (D+50 at this point in 2022, when Republicans won the national vote), and Democrats are shifting to Election Day voting; the state has no in-person early voting, so there is no in-person count to offset it. The official comparison is on the app's panel, so this signal is the turnout picture only. The application deadline passed Oct 27, so the remaining question is the return rate on 384,000 outstanding ballots.
signals.src: Call the Map, Oct 27; TNND/Fox Baltimore, Oct 26
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; TNND is a nonpartisan outlet

signals.title: Wisconsin's absentee returns have caught up with 2022 (2% ahead a week out), but the last county read had Milwaukee down 10% and Dane down 15%
signals.value: Wisconsin Elections Commission report a week before the election (FOX 11, Oct 27): 513,602 absentee ballots returned, 251,092 of them cast early in person, against 503,180 returned a week before the 2022 election; Brown County 24,771, Outagamie 17,038, Winnebago 15,539. The last county comparison (Dairyland Sentinel, data through Oct 23) had the state 5.1% behind 2022 with Milwaukee County down 10.1%, Dane down 14.9% and Madison down 21.3% while Waukesha was up 2.4% and Washington up 22%.
signals.catch: No party registration, so this is turnout only. The statewide gap has closed from 10% behind on Oct 22 to 2% ahead, so the county lag may have closed too; in-person absentee voting runs through Nov 1 and both parties pushed voters away from mail. The county analysis is by Joe Handrick, a former Republican legislator. The part that leans Republican is that the Democratic counties' declines were larger than the suburban Republican counties' on the last county read.
signals.src: FOX 11 (Wisconsin Elections Commission data), Oct 27; Dairyland Sentinel, Oct 23
signals.aff: Official data via a nonpartisan outlet; the county analysis is on a conservative-leaning site by a former Republican legislator

signals.title: Michigan's absentee returns are 4% ahead of 2022 a week out, plus 216,000 early in-person votes that did not exist then
signals.value: Secretary of State release, Oct 27 (7 a.m.): 1,392,170 ballots cast, 18.8% of active registered voters; 1,176,375 absentee ballots returned of 2,154,870 requested (2,016,031 from the permanent list) and 215,795 early in-person votes, more than 134,000 of them in the first two days of statewide early voting. One week before the 2022 election, 1,899,273 absentee ballots had been requested and 1,126,246 returned. Deputy Secretary Edevbie: voters 'are showing enthusiasm for early in-person voting.'
signals.catch: Michigan has no party registration, so this measures turnout, not direction, and the department itself cautions that higher early numbers 'do not necessarily mean' higher overall turnout. About 94% of requests come from the permanent list, which inflates the request count. Early in-person voting runs through Nov 1.

signals.title: Ohio's early electorate flipped from Republican to Democratic by last primary ballot, and LaRose says the state may break its early-vote record
signals.value: Democrats had returned about 94,000 ballots, unaffiliated voters a little more than 67,000 and Republicans nearly 64,000 (by last primary ballot), per the Ohio Capital Journal from Secretary of State data through Oct 12-13; News 5 Cleveland put Democrats at 41% and Republicans at 28% of nearly 230,000 early votes as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024. A week out, 68% of absentee ballots had been returned and Secretary of State LaRose said 'if trendlines continue we could be on track to break another record' (NBC4, Oct 27); the AP's same-point analysis (Oct 26) had Ohio about 30% ahead of 2022.
signals.catch: 2024 was a presidential year, and Ohio Republicans are shifting from mail to later voting: mail requests were 631,079 vs. 871,041 at this point in 2022. 'Party' is the last primary ballot pulled; seniors are more than half of ballots. No newer party breakdown has been published since Oct 15.
signals.src: Ohio Capital Journal (Ohio Secretary of State data), Oct 15; NBC4 Columbus, Oct 27

signals.title: Virginia's early vote has passed 2022's final early total, 1.18 million against 977,000
signals.value: VPAP's count as of Oct 26: 1,183,919 early ballots, just over three-quarters in person and 23% by mail, against 976,558 in all of 2022's early-voting period (DC News Now, Oct 27). The Hill's earlier reading had the state 'about 80% more than at the comparable 2022 stage' as of Oct 22.
signals.catch: Virginia has no party registration, so this is turnout, not direction, and the comparison is to 2022's final, not the same point. Virginia's 2025 governor race already showed a Democratic swing, so high turnout here says less about the national picture. The modeled party lean is in the separate L2 measure.
signals.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; VPAP is a nonpartisan tracker of state data

signals.title: Maine's absentee vote is 37% ahead of 2022 with unaffiliated voters up 58%; the party gap matches 2022's
signals.value: 186,169 ballots through Oct 25 (Call the Map's reading of the Secretary of State file): Democrats 93,254 (up 32% on 2022), Republicans 39,605 (up 28%), unaffiliated 53,310 (up 58%); a D+28.8 gap vs. D+29.4 at the same point in 2022 (and D+17.9 at the same point in 2024 on the Oct 22 reading). In-person absentee ballots are 101,103 (51.3%) and mail 96,001.
signals.catch: Registration is not vote choice. Against 2022 the gap is half a point narrower, so the Democratic reading comes from turnout and the 2024 comparison, and the unaffiliated voters who decide the Collins race are the fastest-growing group. In-person absentee voting ends Oct 29; the state file has not been updated since Oct 25.
signals.src: Call the Map (Maine Secretary of State absentee file), Oct 27
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; affiliation not stated

signals.title: Clark County's mail vote is 6 points less Democratic than at this point in 2022
signals.value: Clark County mail ballots through Oct 25 (Call the Map): 148,516, up 7% on the same point in 2022; Democrats 66,606 (down 3%), Republicans 39,407 (up 13%), unaffiliated 42,502 (up 19%); a D+18.3 gap vs. D+24.1 at the same point in 2022. Ralston's Clark mail count through Monday: D+33,564 against D+35,812 at this point in 2022.
signals.catch: Democrats are shifting from mail to in person, which Ralston's county-wide figures absorb (Clark overall is above D+43,000, almost 13 points, against under 29,000 in 2022); this compares only the mail mode, and mail is about 59% of the vote this year against about half in 2022. Registration is not vote choice.
signals.src: Call the Map (Clark County mail file), Oct 27; Nevada Independent, Oct 27
signals.aff: Independent tracker of the official file; the Nevada Independent is a nonpartisan outlet

signals.title: L2 and McDonald: Democrats' national early-vote edge looks like 2022's, which was not a blue wave
signals.value: Michael McDonald (TNND, Oct 26): more than 30 million ballots; in the party-registration states about 45% Democrats, 30% Republicans, 25% unaffiliated or other; every state he has analyzed is pacing ahead of 2022 except Pennsylvania and Tennessee. Pluribus News (Oct 23): L2's modeled figures 49% Democrats to 34% Republicans, nearly 60% of early voters over 65, and L2's Paul Westcott: 'The best comparison is 2022, and 2022 was not a blue wave,' with Democrats holding 'the same early-vote edge at this point in 2022.' UF Election Lab's Oct 28 count is 35,140,289 ballots; Call the Map's six day-aligned states are 12% ahead of 2022.
signals.catch: L2's party is modeled in states without registration, and the 2022 comparison is Westcott's characterization, not a published same-point table. Democrats' 2022 early-vote edge preceded a national vote they lost by about 3 points, which is why the edge alone says little; the turnout gains are concentrated in states whose Election Day vote was Republican in 2022.
signals.src: TNND/Fox Baltimore, Oct 26; Pluribus News (Reid Wilson), Oct 23; Call the Map, Oct 27
signals.aff: McDonald is a nonpartisan academic; L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor (modeled party)
